question.problem: Find all values of $c$ that satisfy the mean value theorem for integrals for  $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ on the interval $[0,4].$
question.worked_solution:
Applying the mean value theorem for integrals, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c)(b-a) & ={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ f(c) & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4-0}{\int }_{0}^{4}\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{4}\cdot (\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3/2})|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\frac{2}{3}\cdot {4}^{3/2}-\frac{2}{3}\cdot {0}^{3/2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{16}{3} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the expression for $f(x)$ to solve for the value of $c:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c) & =\frac{4}{3} \\ \sqrt{c} & =\frac{4}{3} \\ c & =\frac{16}{9}\end{aligned}
$$
